note: Bands on the 1-6 scale (no neutral midpoint, forced-choice). The quadrant cutoff is 3.5: the original 1-7 ECR-R midpoint (4) rescaled proportionally to 1-6 ((4-1)/6*5+1). ECR-R has no official categorical cutoffs, so the two dimension scores are stored and shown alongside the quadrant, and results within near_boundary of the cutoff are flagged.

bands.label: Secure in the bond
bands.description: You generally trust a partner's care without needing frequent reassurance, and you don't dwell on fears of abandonment.

bands.label: Occasionally reassurance-seeking
bands.description: You're mostly settled, but under stress or ambiguity you can spiral into worry about a partner's feelings.

bands.label: High need for reassurance
bands.description: You often worry about a partner's love or commitment, and closeness can come with real anxiety about losing it.

bands.label: Comfortable with closeness
bands.description: You're at ease sharing feelings and depending on a partner, and you don't need much distance to feel safe.

bands.label: Selective about closeness
bands.description: You open up with the right person and at the right pace, but there are real limits to how much dependence feels comfortable.

bands.label: Prefers independence
bands.description: Closeness and dependence feel uncomfortable. You tend to rely on yourself and keep some emotional distance, even in committed relationships.

combined_patterns.label: Secure
combined_patterns.description: You're comfortable with both closeness and independence, and you trust relationships without excessive worry or a need for distance.

combined_patterns.label: Anxious-preoccupied
combined_patterns.description: You deeply value closeness but often worry about whether it's returned or at risk.

combined_patterns.label: Dismissive-avoidant
combined_patterns.description: You value independence and self-sufficiency. You don't fear closeness exactly; you just don't prioritise or need it.

combined_patterns.label: Fearful-avoidant
combined_patterns.description: You want closeness but distrust it, pulled between wanting connection and protecting yourself from getting hurt by it.
